**"Power Level Prophecy"**

The gang had gathered in Shubie-Ommada's lab for what was supposed to be a routine scanner calibration. Shubie had been running diagnostics on some ancient Avalice tech when his instruments started screaming.

"Uh, guys?" His voice cracked. "I think I just intercepted a temporal distress beacon."

"Temporal?" Lilac leaned over the console, her purple quills bristling. "Like... time travel?"

"Like something's sending a message *backward* through time," Shubie confirmed, his fingers flying across the keyboard. "It's heavily encoded, but I'm getting fragments. Power readings. *Really* specific power readings."

Carol cracked her knuckles. "How bad we talking?"

What came next wasn't a number Shubie could even say out loud at first. He just pointed at the screen.

The silence was absolute.

"That's... that can't be right," Lilac whispered. "That's not even—what *is* that?"

"999 decillion," Shubie read slowly. "The beacon's from about fifty years in the future. It's tagged with a signature match: Milla Basset."

The door to the lab burst open. Milla herself trotted in, her tails wagging, completely oblivious. "Hiiii everyone! I smelled cookies from Shubie's kitchen and I—why do you all look like you just saw a ghost?"

Carol's jaw was on the floor. Lilac was gripping the console so hard her knuckles had turned white. Shubie was sweating profusely.

"Milla," Lilac said very carefully, "what's the biggest explosion you've ever caused?"

"Um... when I accidentally knocked over all the TNT barrels in Relic Ruins?" Milla tilted her head. "That was pretty big! Why?"

"And where would you say your power level is *right now*?"

Milla's tails drooped slightly. "Oh... maybe like... 47? I've been slacking on training lately..."

The collective WHAT? was deafening.

Shubie pulled up the full data. "The beacon's clean. No corruption, no errors. Future-Milla doesn't just hit 999 decillion—she *sustains* it. For *days*. There's a secondary message that decrypts to..." He scrolled. His expression cycled through confusion, amusement, and then quiet horror. "Oh no."

"Oh no what?" Carol demanded.

"She... she does it *by accident*."

Milla blinked innocently. "By accident? I'm not sure I understand."

Shubie read from the translated log: "'Attempted to help Lilac move a large rock. Got too enthusiastic with tails. Accidentally opened a rift to a dimension made of catnip. It's been fifty-three days. Send snacks. The dimensional walls are very sparkly. I don't think I can come home.'"

There was a beat.

Then Carol started laughing—actually cackling—and she couldn't stop. "SHE PUNCHES A HOLE IN REALITY BY BEING *NICE*?"

"It seems future-Milla's kindness powers scale exponentially," Shubie said, dead serious. "Eventually, past a certain threshold, helping is literally reality-breaking."

Lilac had her face in her hands. "We've been worried about the wrong threats this whole time. We need to *contain* Milla."

"Contain me?" Milla's ears flopped. "But I haven't done anything!"
